# Checkbox

Figma: [03e. Checkbox](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-900) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-23

A binary selection control for multiple-choice options where the user can pick zero, one, or many. Visually a small box that becomes filled with a check (or dash for indeterminate) when selected. Used for terms acceptance, multi-select filters, settings toggles where the choice is yes/no, and bulk select-all patterns.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/checkbox/reference.png`

### Checkbox Indicator

The square box atom of a checkbox with checked, indeterminate and disabled visuals.

Level: atom · Part of: Checkbox

Use when:
- Inside Checkbox
- Select-all cells in table headers or rows where the row is the label

Don't use when:
- A labelled choice: use Checkbox
- Exclusive choices: use Radio Indicator inside Radio

Accessibility: Standalone use needs an accessible name and a 24dp+ tap region; sm is 16dp.

### Checkbox

A labelled checkbox for independent yes or no choices applied on submit, such as accepting terms or multi-select filters.

Level: organism · Contains: Checkbox Indicator · Part of: Checkbox Group

Use when:
- Accepting terms, risk disclosure or Sharia terms before investing
- Multi-select filters (Residential, Commercial, Industrial)
- Select-all with partial selection: State=indeterminate

Don't use when:
- Only one option may be chosen: use Radio inside Radio Group
- The setting applies instantly on tap: use Switch
- Several related checkboxes under one label: use Checkbox Group

Accessibility: The whole label is the tap target; avoid sm on touch screens and never pre-check consent boxes.

### Checkbox Group

A group label, a vertical stack of Checkbox items and a helper line for multi-select questions.

Level: organism · Contains: Checkbox, Checkbox Indicator

Use when:
- Multi-select KYC questions such as investment goals or sources of income
- Notification topics (new deals, payouts, account updates) chosen together and saved on submit

Don't use when:
- Exactly one answer: use Radio Group
- Instant on/off settings: use Switch rows in an ActionList
- Long option lists: use Multi-select field

Accessibility: Expose the group label as the group name so each option is announced in context.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Checkbox is the standard control for yes/no choices when multiple selections are independent - each checkbox represents one option that's either on or off, regardless of its neighbors. Compare with Radio (one-of-many): Radio enforces exclusivity; Checkbox does not.

On Safqah, Checkbox shows up on: terms-and-conditions acceptance during signup ("I agree to the Sharia compliance terms"), multi-select deal filters ("Filter by: Residential / Commercial / Industrial"), notification preferences ("Email me about: New deals / Distributions / Account updates"), and bulk-select tables (header checkbox toggles all rows).

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Checkbox follows the same atomic pattern as the rest of the form family. The Indicator atom handles the box itself; the Checkbox organism composes it with a label and optional helper text.

Atom - Checkbox Indicator · 21 variants

The box itself. Variants: 3 sizes × 7 states (unchecked / hover / focus / checked / indeterminate / disabled-unchecked / disabled-checked). Direction-agnostic - the indicator is symmetric and looks identical in LTR and RTL. Reused inside the Checkbox organism as an exposed instance.

Organism - Checkbox · 42 variants

Composes Indicator + Label (text) + optional Helper text below. Variants: 3 sizes × 7 states × 2 directions. The Direction axis flips the indicator and label order - LTR shows [box label]; RTL shows [label box]. Indicator is exposed so state can be controlled through the organism props.

### Sizes

Three sizes match the surrounding form density. lg for primary touch contexts (mobile-first), md for standard desktop density, sm for compact contexts like dense tables.

Large (24dp box, font 16dp)

Primary forms on mobile - terms acceptance, signup consents, multi-select on hero deal cards. Pairs with lg Input and lg Button. Meets WCAG 2.5.5 AAA touch target (24dp box + label tap area = comfortably >44dp).

Medium (20dp box, font 14dp)

Standard desktop density - settings forms, filter panels, notification preferences. The most common choice for dense desktop UIs.

Small (16dp box, font 14dp)

Compact contexts only - bulk-select tables, inline list filters where vertical space is tight. Use sparingly on mobile (box itself is small but label tap area can extend the hit zone).

### States

Seven states cover the full interaction lifecycle. Indeterminate is a special state for "select-all" patterns where some (but not all) children are checked - the dash signals partial selection.

unchecked

Default empty state. Box has bg/surface fill with 1.5dp border/default border. User taps to check.

hover

Cursor/touch hover. Border switches to border/strong for a subtle interactive cue without committing to a state change.

focus

Keyboard focus or pre-tap. 2dp border/focus ring outside the box, visible even when the box is empty. Important for accessibility.

checked

Selected. Box fills with bg/brand/primary (green), white check icon. The primary "yes" affordance.

indeterminate

Partial selection. Box fills with bg/brand/primary, white dash (instead of check). Used on parent checkboxes when SOME but not all children are checked. Tapping moves to checked.

disabled-unchecked

Inert empty state. Box uses bg/disabled (gray), label text/muted. Use when the option is unavailable in current context.

disabled-checked

Inert selected state. Box uses bg/disabled, muted check icon. Use when the value is locked to true by another control (e.g. "always enabled" features).

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Checkbox flips its internal layout for Arabic context. In LTR the indicator sits before the label; in RTL the indicator moves to the trailing edge (after the label) so the visual flow reads naturally right-to-left.

LTR

Default. Indicator on the leading (left) edge, label after. Standard for English contexts.

RTL

Arabic context. Label first, indicator on the trailing (visually right) edge. Matches Arabic reading flow throughout the Safqah app.

### Code examples

How to consume Checkbox in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic Checkbox

```dart
// Standard checkbox for terms acceptance
SafqahCheckbox(
  value: _agreedToTerms,
  label: 'I agree to the Sharia compliance terms',
  onChanged: (value) {
    setState(() => _agreedToTerms = value ?? false);
  },
)
```

### Flutter - multi-select filter

```dart
// Multiple independent options
Column(
  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
  children: DealCategory.values.map((category) {
    return SafqahCheckbox(
      value: _selectedCategories.contains(category),
      label: category.localizedName,
      onChanged: (checked) {
        setState(() {
          if (checked == true) {
            _selectedCategories.add(category);
          } else {
            _selectedCategories.remove(category);
          }
        });
      },
    );
  }).toList(),
)
```

### Flutter - select-all with indeterminate

```dart
// Header checkbox controls children
final allSelected = _selectedItems.length == _items.length;
final someSelected = _selectedItems.isNotEmpty && !allSelected;

SafqahCheckbox(
  value: allSelected,
  indeterminate: someSelected,
  label: 'Select all (${_selectedItems.length}/${_items.length})',
  onChanged: (checked) {
    setState(() {
      if (checked == true) {
        _selectedItems = Set.from(_items);
      } else {
        _selectedItems.clear();
      }
    });
  },
)
```

### Flutter - RTL Arabic context

```dart
// Arabic locale - checkbox flips to indicator-on-right
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahCheckbox(
    value: _agreed,
    label: 'أوافق على الشروط والأحكام',  // "I agree to the terms"
    onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _agreed = v ?? false),
  ),
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Independent multi-select: Use Checkbox when each option is independent - selecting one doesn't affect others (notification types, deal categories, language preferences).
- **Don't** · Independent multi-select: Don't use Checkbox for mutually exclusive choices (one investment plan, one payment method). Use Radio - Checkbox semantics imply independent toggles, breaking user expectations.
- **Do** · Select-all pattern: Use indeterminate state on the parent when SOME children are selected. Visual dash signals "partial selection" - users intuit they can tap to complete or clear.
- **Don't** · Select-all pattern: Don't show the parent as unchecked when some children are selected - it misleads users about the current state. Don't invent a "third state" for indeterminate; reserved for select-all only.
- **Do** · Arabic RTL form: RTL direction. Label first (reads right-to-left), indicator on the trailing edge. Matches Arabic reading flow on Nafath, signup forms, and settings.
- **Don't** · Arabic RTL form: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts. Indicator on the wrong side breaks visual flow - Arabic users scan right-to-left, expect the actionable element on the trailing edge of the label.
- **Do** · Locked / unavailable option: Disabled-checked state when a feature is forced on by the user's tier or by a parent setting (e.g. "Email security alerts" can't be disabled on enterprise accounts). Clear visual signal that the choice is locked.
- **Don't** · Locked / unavailable option: Don't leave a locked option in active checked state - user will tap it expecting to toggle, get no feedback, and assume the app is broken. Disabled visual is the contract.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Built upon the v1 "Selections" component - kept the same visual language (white check on green, indeterminate dash, focus ring outside the box) but split into proper atomic decomposition. v1 was one combined component for Checkbox + Radio; v2 splits them into separate pages with shared visual conventions but independent component sets.

> **Info:** Checkbox and Radio share the same indicator dimensions (16/20/24dp), same border weights (1.5dp normal, 2dp focus), same focus ring placement (OUTSIDE the box). Radio differs only in: circular shape (Radius/Full), filled dot instead of check icon. Means the two controls feel like a coherent family across forms.

> **Info:** Indicator is exposed as a nested instance on every Checkbox organism variant. Atom-level state (the State prop on Indicator) can be controlled through the parent, OR through the variant axis on the organism - both are wired in.

> **Info:** Direction axis on the organism is the ONLY axis that handles RTL. The Indicator atom is direction-agnostic (the box is symmetric). This keeps the variant count manageable - 21 indicator variants × 2 directions would be redundant for a symmetric box.

> **Info:** Help text Show Helper boolean ships as false by default. Most checkboxes are simple - just label + box. Helper text is for terms-acceptance where you need a "Read the full terms" link below, or for explanatory text under settings checkboxes.

> **Warning:** WCAG WARNING - sm size has a 16dp box, below the WCAG 2.5.5 AA minimum of 24dp. The label tap area extends the effective target, but on touch-only contexts the box alone is too small. Flagged for use only in dense desktop UIs.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the form family. Label uses IBM Plex Sans Regular since Font/Family/Base resolves to IBM Plex Sans Arabic (not installed). Font/Size and Font/Line-Height are bound to font/size/N and font/line-height/N variables on every text node.

> **Warning:** Border weight 1.5dp is a raw px value - there's no stroke-width primitive in DS. Same flag as other components. The 2dp focus ring is also raw. If you add a stroke-width primitive system later, rebind these.
